quote: the rising rising electricity cost. I talked to somebody, like, maybe two years ago, and I just kinda regret not doing it then
stewart_read: Zachary hands the rep a strong emotional anchor (regret + prior contact) but the rep pivots straight to a tax-credit factual answer instead of digging into the regret.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically saving the emotional hook for the bill-flip later, but no later moment reuses this regret.
coaching_implication: Reflect the regret back: 'so this is your second look — let's make sure this time doesn't slip by' ties urgency to his own words.

quote: Now it's, like, $3.53 90. So, like, edging up on 400.
stewart_read: Bill captured but rep responds with a generic 'Wow, okay' and 'we can definitely get that lower' rather than flipping it into villain framing against the utility.
coaching_implication: Use the number itself as leverage: 'that's money going straight to AES every month with nothing to show for it' — schema's objection_inversion pattern.

quote: Trying to find a better a better look at it. This app sucks.
stewart_read: Clear friction signal on the app path; schema calls for pivoting to verbal read-back within 2 minutes, not letting the struggle continue.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the customer competent enough to eventually succeed (he does eventually send a photo), which he does — but the time cost was still high.
coaching_implication: At first sign of 'this app sucks,' offer: 'no worries, just read me the numbers off the bar graph instead.'

quote: I'm I did get that photo. It's only showing me, like, five months.
stewart_read: Second friction touch on the same bill-photo path; rep again asks for more screenshots rather than closing out with what's already captured (Jan/Feb kWh already given verbally).
coaching_implication: Rep already has verbal kWh figures at 04:48 — could have told customer that's sufficient and deferred the rest to the closer visit.

quote: it's my usage is, like, almost almost double... 1,500 to 2,300
stewart_read: Customer is animated and self-analyzing his own usage spike — a live curiosity moment about why his bill is climbing.
coaching_implication: Rep responds with 'Yeah... I could see that here' — a missed chance to tie this spike directly to the appointment value ('that's exactly the kind of shift our design will map out for you Monday').

quote: Well, I mean, will you be able to send me some program information in the meantime?
stewart_read: This is a version of the send-info-early ask; rep holds the hard rule on the design but caves partially by offering to email 'basics of the program,' a softer version of the same risk.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be reading this as low-risk since it's general info, not the actual design proposal, which is a defensible partial concession.
coaching_implication: Even 'program basics' emails dilute the appointment's exclusivity — better to redirect fully: 'everything gets explained live so it actually makes sense in the context of your numbers.'

quote: Yeah. Let's tentatively plan for that, and I'll let you know if that doesn't work.
stewart_read: No firm 'is that fair?' handshake or locked commitment — the appointment closes as explicitly provisional on the customer's own terms.
coaching_implication: Rep should have anchored: 'let's go ahead and lock Monday 3:30 — I'll hold that hour for you, does that work?' rather than accepting the tentative framing passively.
